Thank you for sharing that history. To better understand your new movement disorder, can you describe exactly how your tremors or jerking movements have changed since starting this medication?

Also, have you noticed any stiffness, shaking when holding a position, or a feeling that your limbs are moving on their own?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is helpful. Did the movements start immediately after your first dose, or did they develop gradually over the past two months? Also, does taking an extra dose make the shaking worse?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC), Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP), and Serum Prolactin level.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-Induced Acute Dystonia (likely misidentified by patient as akathisia; however, given the description of restlessness, pacing, and fidgeting without mention of sustained muscle contractions or dystonic posturing, this is actually Drug-Induced Akathisia).

REQUEST TEST: None needed for this clinical presentation.
REQUEST IMAGES: None needed.

You described symptoms of inner restlessness and an inability to sit still (pacing, fidgeting), which are classic signs of akathisia, a common side effect of risperidone. This is not an emergency, but it requires adjusting your medication dose or adding a beta-blocker. Please return in 2 weeks to review your test results and discuss treatment adjustments.
